newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port workers end nationwide strike - union.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port workers end nationwide strike - union.

text.p: Brazil port workers ended to a 48-hour nationwide strike and said they would return to work immediately after a partial agreement at a Santos steel mill was reached with management, a union official said on Friday.
"The strike is over. Workers will go back to work at most ports this evening," Orlandino Custodio, Director of Social Assistance at the National Federation of Port Workers told Reuters.
Custodio said the union ended the protest after reaching a "partial agreement" with representatives of the Santos-based steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa).
For two weeks the Cosipa terminal has been virtually paralized after the company decided to use its own employees to load and unload ships and stop using stevedore union members.
Under the terms of Friday's agreement, members of the stevedore union and Cosipa employees will alternate in loading and unloading ships that dock at the Cospia terminal, Custodio said.
He said talks between Cosipa management and the National Stevedore Federation would continue on Tuesday April 22.
Monday April 21 is a national holiday in Brazil.
Officials said the national strike, which began at 0700 today, had had little effect on agricultural commodities and that many ports had operated normally.
